issues.legal_issue: A public corporation whose employee is barred from appointment as a competent authority has an independent grievance entitling it to challenge that restriction.
material_facts: The High Court directed that the competent authority could not be an employee of the corporation.
The corporation was directly affected by that direction and filed a special leave petition.
issues.conclusion: The corporation had an independent cause of grievance and could file the special leave petition.
issues.legal_principle: A party with an independent grievance against an order may challenge that order; the judgment identifies no particular statutory provision or earlier case for this holding.

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is a special leave appeal challenging a court order.
predicates.order_restricts_corporation_appointment_: The challenged order restricts who may be appointed to perform a function connected with the corporation's project.
predicates.corporation_is_directly_affected: The corporation is directly affected by the restriction imposed by the order.
predicates.corporation_may_challenge_order: The corporation is entitled to challenge the order.

issues.definition: When a special leave appeal challenges a restriction on appointment options that directly affects a corporation, the corporation may challenge the order.

issues.legal_issue: Employment by a public corporation alone does not disqualify a person from appointment as a competent authority.
material_facts: The appointee was an employee of the corporation that benefited from the pipeline project.
The Act contained no provision prohibiting the appointment of a corporation employee as competent authority.
The competent authority performed varied duties under the Act, which could provide relevant experience for determining compensation.
issues.conclusion: A person cannot be disqualified merely because that person is an employee of the corporation; a challenge to an individual appointee's bias requires sufficient material beyond the fact of employment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(a) and 7 to 10 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 contain no prohibition on appointing a corporation employee, and the Act assigns the competent authority diverse duties. The court distinguished Metropolitan Properties Co. Ltd. v. Lannon, G. Sarana v. University of Lucknow, and International Airports Authority of India v. K.D. & Anr.; it rejected extending the bias theory to exclude a person merely because the person draws a salary from a public corporation or government body.

predicates.appointment_under_pipeline_right_of_user: The proceeding concerns appointment of a competent authority under a law governing acquisition of pipeline rights of user in land.
predicates.appointee_is_public_corporation_employee: The appointed person is an employee of the public corporation benefiting from the project.
predicates.no_individual_bias_material_beyond_emplo: There is no material supporting bias by the individual appointee apart from that person's employment by the corporation.
predicates.employment_alone_does_not_make_appointme: The appointee is not disqualified solely because of employment by the corporation.

issues.definition: If a pipeline-right-of-user appointment is challenged and the only basis for alleging bias is the appointee's employment by the public corporation, that employment alone does not invalidate the appointment.

issues.legal_issue: An appointment as competent authority is invalid when the appointee is personally litigating the same compensation dispute, creating a well-founded apprehension of bias.
material_facts: The appointee later filed a writ petition in her own name challenging the compensation award made in favour of the person claiming compensation.
The appointee was therefore herself a litigating party in the same matter in which she could determine compensation.
The High Court had found the appointment invalid, and the Supreme Court considered the resulting apprehension of bias well founded.
issues.conclusion: The appointment was invalid in these circumstances because the appointee's personal litigation in the same matter gave rise to a well-founded apprehension of bias.
issues.legal_principle: The rule that no one may be a judge in their own cause concerns personal interest in the matter to be adjudicated. The test is whether a litigant could reasonably apprehend that bias might operate against them, rather than whether bias actually affected the decision. The court distinguished Metropolitan Properties Co. Ltd. v. Lannon, G. Sarana v. University of Lucknow, and International Airports Authority of India v. K.D. & Anr., while accepting that sufficient material may establish bias against an individual appointee.

predicates.appeal_challenges_invalidation_of_author: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision that invalidated an appointment as competent authority.
predicates.appointee_is_personally_litigating_same_: The appointee is personally a litigant in the same dispute that the appointee may decide.
predicates.apprehension_of_bias_is_well_founded: The circumstances give a litigant a reasonable, fact-based apprehension that bias may affect the decision.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an invalidated authority appointment, the appointee is personally litigating the same dispute, and the resulting apprehension of bias is well founded, the appointment is invalid.
